pr_title: fix(rust,python): Improve error message in DataFrame constructor
pr_body:
Fixes #6714 

New error message reads:

> exceptions.ShapeError: Could not create a new DataFrame from Series. The Series have different lengths: found length 2 for Series named "a" and length 1 for Series named "b".

Comments on my Rust implementation are very welcome - I'm sure there's a cleaner way to do this.

issue_context.title: Badly formatted error message when invalid data passed to `DataFrame` constructor
issue_context.body:
### Polars version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Issue description

See example.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

data = {"a": [100, 101], "b": [102], "c": [103, 104, 105]}

df = pl.DataFrame(data)
```

Results in:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/home/stijn/.cache/pypoetry/virtualenvs/bakplan-calculator-TjseP0Di-py3.11/lib/python3.11/site-packages/polars/utils.py", line 393, in wrapper
    return fn(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/stijn/.cache/pypoetry/virtualenvs/bakplan-calculator-TjseP0Di-py3.11/lib/python3.11/site-packages/polars/internals/dataframe/frame.py", line 329, in __init__
    self._df = dict_to_pydf(
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/stijn/.cache/pypoetry/virtualenvs/bakplan-calculator-TjseP0Di-py3.11/lib/python3.11/site-packages/polars/internals/construction.py", line 697, in dict_to_pydf
    return PyDataFrame(data_series)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
exceptions.ShapeError: Could not create a new DataFrame from Series. The Series have different lengths. Got [shape: (2,)
Series: 'a' [i64]
[
        100
        101
], shape: (1,)
Series: 'b' [i64]
[
        102
], shape: (3,)
Series: 'c' [i64]
[
        103
        104
        105
]]
```

It prints all the data! Now imagine you actually pass some larger dataframe, it will consume your whole logs.


### Expected behavior

The error message shouldn't print all the data. It should probably only print the fact that the Series have different lengths.

comments:
> It should probably only print the fact that the Series have different lengths.

why not print the lengths as well?

I considered that, but let's say you have a 100 columns of length 10, and there's one mistake in there, then you still get a hundred lines looking like:

```
10
10
10
10
11
10
...
10
10
10
```

And you have to find the one shape that's different.

I just don't think the size of our error messages should scale with the size of the input data in any way.

Thanks for explaining - how about just printing the first one, and the first one which differs?

Something like
```
The Series have different lengths: found length 2 at index 0, and length 1 and index 1
```
Then it wouldn't scale with the size of the input, but would still give more info about what's wrong
I think that would be a great solution! I'll see if I can make that happen in Rust 😄

review_comments: This unwrap should be safe, as this path can only be triggered when we're already at index 2 of the `series_cols` vector.
I think we should get the first name only during raising an error. The happy path should not be slowed down by giving extra error information.

You're right. Changed it around, should be good to go now!

This specific line was moved up from line 251; we need to get the `name` anyway for checking duplicate names.
